name: Battle of the Pyramids

edges.name: Ibrahim Bey’s army across the Nile →

phases.title: The two armies take their places
phases.text: The French formed five divisional squares in echelon, Desaix on the right and Bon on the left beside the Nile. Murad Bey fixed his right at fortified Embabeh and his left at Biktil, with the Mamluk cavalry between them.

phases.title: The French advance and occupy Biktil
phases.text: The French moved south in echelon, each division holding its square, and Desaix sent a detachment to occupy the village of Biktil on Murad Bey’s left, where he had placed additional guns.

phases.title: Mamluk cavalry charge the squares
phases.text: Murad meant to hold the French on his fortified flanks and strike their centre with cavalry, and repeated charges were directed against the squares.

phases.title: The mass assault of about 15:30
phases.text: Murad ordered his defterdar, Ayyub Bey, to lead a mass assault. The divisions of Desaix, Reynier and Dugua held firm and repelled the horsemen with musketry and artillery.

phases.title: The Mamluks attack Desaix’s detachment
phases.text: After the assault failed, some of the Mamluks then attempted to attack Desaix’s detached force near Biktil, but without success.

phases.title: Bon’s columns storm Embabeh
phases.text: Near the river Bon’s division formed attack columns and stormed Embabeh. The garrison broke and many fled into the Nile, where hundreds drowned.

phases.title: Murad escapes towards Upper Egypt
phases.text: Murad’s losses were far heavier than the French, with thousands killed or wounded, Ayyub Bey among them. Murad, wounded in the cheek, got away with several thousand cavalry to Upper Egypt.

note: The accounts give the French order from right to left, the Nile on their left and their advance to the south, so the river is drawn on the east. The distances, the exact lie of the two villages and the places of the squares are not given and are placed by judgement.
